name: Diwali
description: The festival of lights, symbolizing the victory of light over darkness and good over evil. Homes are decorated with diyas and rangoli.

name: Holi
description: The festival of colors, celebrating the arrival of spring and the triumph of good over evil. People play with colors and share sweets.

name: Navaratri
description: A nine-night festival dedicated to the worship of the Goddess Durga in her various forms. Includes Garba, Dandiya, and elaborate pujas.

name: Maha Shivaratri
description: The great night of Shiva, a solemn festival marking the remembrance of overcoming darkness and ignorance. Devotees fast and chant Om Namah Shivaya.

name: Ganesh Chaturthi
description: A ten-day festival marking the birth of Lord Ganesha, the remover of obstacles. Clay idols are installed and immersed on the final day.

name: Ram Navami
description: Celebrates the birth of Lord Rama, the seventh avatar of Vishnu. Devotees recite the Ramayana and visit temples.

name: Janmashtami
description: Celebrates the birth of Lord Krishna, the eighth avatar of Vishnu. Marked by Dahi Handi, bhajans, and midnight celebrations.

name: Makar Sankranti / Pongal
description: Marks the sun's transition into Capricorn. Celebrated as Pongal in Tamil Nadu, Uttarayan in Gujarat. Kites, bonfires, and harvest thanksgiving.

name: Ugadi / Gudi Padwa
description: Hindu New Year for South and West India. Homes are cleaned and decorated, and Ugadi Pachadi (a mix of six tastes) is prepared.

name: Raksha Bandhan
description: Celebrates the bond between brothers and sisters. Sisters tie a sacred thread (rakhi) on their brother's wrist.

name: Dussehra / Vijayadashami
description: Marks the victory of Lord Rama over Ravana and Goddess Durga over Mahishasura. Grand effigies of Ravana are burnt across India.

name: Hanuman Jayanti
description: Celebrates the birth of Lord Hanuman, the devoted servant of Lord Rama. Special prayers and Hanuman Chalisa recitation.

name: Karva Chauth
description: A one-day festival where married women fast from sunrise to moonrise for the longevity of their husbands.

name: Guru Purnima
description: A day to honor spiritual teachers and mentors. Falls on the full moon day (Purnima) in the month of Ashadha.

name: Chhath Puja
description: An ancient Vedic festival dedicated to the Sun God. Devotees stand in water and offer prayers at sunrise and sunset.

name: Vasant Panchami
description: Celebrates the arrival of spring. Devoted to Goddess Saraswati, the deity of knowledge, music, and art. People wear yellow.

name: Onam
description: Kerala's harvest festival celebrating the homecoming of King Mahabali. Famous for Pookalam, boat races, and Onam Sadya feast.

name: Holika Dahan
description: The night before Holi. Bonfires are lit to symbolize the burning of the demoness Holika and the triumph of devotee Prahlada.
